How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website
as noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting
day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for their consideration,
but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after 4:00 P.M. will be
forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
Public Comment.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – JUNE 2024

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2023-2024 Adopted Investment

  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as

  Recommended Action:

  D. ORDINANCE NO. 709: AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATING TO EMERGENCY SHELTERS, GROUP HOMES, LOWER BARRIER
  NAVIGATION CENTERS, SUPPORTIVE AND TRANSITIONAL HOUSING
  (ZTA24-003) – SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  Ordinance No. 709 was approved at introduction by a 4-0 vote of the City
  Council at the July 2, 2024, City Council meeting. If adopted, the Ordinance
  would become effective 30 days after adoption. The Fiscal Year 2023-2024
  Adopted Budget includes the cost for required legal publication (Account No.
  121-702-00-65-000) and codification (Account No. 121-702-00-22-000) of the
  ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendments were reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA). An Initial Study/Negative Declaration (IS/ND) was prepared
  for the 2021-2029 Housing Element, as required by the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA), Public Resources Code (PRC) Section 21000 et seq., the CEQA

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 16, 2024  3
   Guidelines, and the City of San Gabriel Local Guidelines for Implementing CEQA.
  The Element establishes objectives, policies, and programs to assist the City in
  achieving state-mandated housing goals. No formal land use changes or physical
  development are proposed at this time and future land use and physical
  development would require separate environmental evaluation.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  709 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Approving Planning Case No. ZTA23-004, Amending Title XV,
  Chapter 153 (Zoning) Relating to Emergency Shelters, Group Homes, Lower
  Barrier Navigation Center, Supportive and Transitional Housing.”

  E. PURCHASE OF A NEW NEXTECH IN-ROADWAY WARNING LIGHT
  PEDESTRIAN CROSSWALK SYSTEM AT THE INTERSECTION OF DEL MAR
  AVENUE AND LIVE OAK STREET FOR A TOTAL COST OF $28,612.33

  One of the major goals of the Office of Traffic Safety (OTS) is to reduce the
  number of people killed and injured in crashes involving pedestrians and
  bicyclists. The grant-funded strategies include the purchase of an illuminated
  crosswalk at the intersection of Del Mar Avenue and Live Oak Street. An
  associated goal of OTS is to provide local law enforcement agencies with grant
  funding in order to purchase the necessary equipment to meet the goals and
  objectives of the Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety Program. The adopted Fiscal
  Year 2023-2024 budget includes $55,000 in the Office of Traffic Safety
  Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety Program (Grant #PS24033), Account No. 147-751-
  00-21-146. $28,612.33 from the account will be used to fund the purchase of
  the new NexTech illuminated crosswalk.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to approve
  the purchase of the NexTech System in the amount of $28,612.33 from the
  Office of Traffic Safety Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety Grant Program Grant,
  Account No. 147-751-00-21-146.

  F. PURCHASE OF PATROL RIFLES FOR THE SAN GABRIEL POLICE
  DEPARTMENT FROM LC ACTION POLICE SUPPLY, IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $23,811.63

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 16, 2024  4
   The San Gabriel Police Department purchased Colt M4 Commandos in
  December of 2005 and April of 2007. These patrol rifles have been in service for
  more than 18 years. The recommended service life of a moderately-used patrol
  rifle is approximately 15 years per manufacturer standards. In addition, the
  Department’s rifles undergo high usage because of the mandated training for
  all sworn personnel. Funding for the purchase of the new rifles is budgeted in
  Fiscal Year 2024-2025 under General Funds Special Project Account No. 124-
  751-15-99-173. The total purchase price for the new patrol rifles is $23,811.63.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to approve
  the purchase of (20) Colt M5 Patrol Rifles, Model No. CM-556-10H-M5A from
  LC Action Police Supply.

  G. SAN GABRIEL POLICE DEPARTMENT OUTDOOR LOCKER PROJECT FOR
  POLICE OFFICERS’ EQUIPMENT IN THE AMOUNT OF $35,000.00

  San Gabriel Police Department (SGPD) officers carry a growing array of
  specialized equipment and gear in their Police equipment bags, including
  ammunition, tactical gear, first aid kits, personal protective equipment, and
  other essential items. Currently, these bags are stored on the lower level of the
  SGPD station in wooden lockers that were installed over twenty years ago.
  These wooden lockers were not designed for commercial and heavy use and
  have limited space. Many of the lockers have sustained damage beyond repair
  due to long-time use and wear and tear. The total purchase price for thirty-two
  lockers is $21,127.11. Public Works staff will prep and pour the raised cement
  slab, which the lockers will sit on. The weather-resistant self-standing awning
  has an approximate cost of $13,000.00. The project will not exceed $35,000.00.
  The cost of the project will not impact the Police general fund and will be
  supported by the Development Impact Fund, Account No. 124-751-40-97-610.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to approve
  the purchase of thirty-two (32) lockers, Model No. 71024GY-A, from Salsbury

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 16, 2024  5
   Industries, the purchase of a weather-resistant awning, and for Public Works
  staff to prep and pour a raised cement slab.

  H. FIRST AMENDMENT TO MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN
  GABRIEL VALLEY COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS RELATED TO THE
  REGIONAL FOOD RECOVERY PROGRAM

  The San Gabriel Valley Council of Government (SGVCOG) has established and
  is administering a Regional Food Recovery Program to maximize resources by
  enhancing the capacity of local food recovery organizations to recover edible
  food waste. Additionally, the Program provides outreach and educational
  activities to promote compliance with Senate Bill 1383. The First Amendment
  would allow the City to utilize $15,000 of Senate Bill 1383 Local Assistance Grant
  Program funds to continue supporting the Regional Food Recovery Program
  implemented by the SGVCOG. There is no fiscal impact to the General Fund.
  Additional participation in the Regional Food Recovery expansion will be
  funded by the City’s awarded funds from CalRecycle’s SB 1383 Local Assistance
  Grant Program in Budget Account No. 124-800-57-96-584.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the First Amendment to the Memorandum of Agreement between the City of
  San Gabriel and the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments and approve a
  purchase order for $15,000 with the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments.

  I. PURCHASE OF LUCAS 3 MECHANICAL CPR DEVICE IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $31,364.12

  The Lucas CPR device is a significant improvement for paramedics in the field
  of emergency medical care. In addition to integration with functions of cardiac
  monitor-defibrillators, LUCAS provides consistent chest compressions during
  CPR, maintaining the recommended depth and rate. The device ensures
  uninterrupted chest compressions, even during patient transport. This
  consistency is crucial for maintaining blood flow to vital organs and increasing
  chances of survival. Stryker, Incorporated in cooperation with Fire Department
  staff, has provided the loan of a Lucas device for use on Rescue Ambulance 51
  for nearly 18 months. The cost of acquiring a LUCAS 3 CPR device is $31,364.12
  and funds are available in Fire Department Account No. 121-761-00-21-000.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 16, 2024  6
   The purchase price includes accessories such as batteries, charger, and ongoing
  service.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager or designee
  to issue a purchase order for one LUCAS CPR device as detailed in Attachment
  A, under a cooperative purchasing agreement and in compliance with City of
  San Gabriel Purchasing Policy.

  J. RENEWAL OF DIGITAL EMS ELECTRONIC PATIENT CARE RECORD (EPCR)
  CONTRACT

  As a Public Agency Paramedic Provider Agency, the San Gabriel Fire
  Department must generate and submit a Patient Care Record (PCR) for each
  patient contact made in the delivery of emergency medical service. The
  requirement to submit this data in an electronic format (ePCR) has been in Los
  Angeles County EMS Agency Policy Ref. 607 since 2009. To meet this
  requirement the Fire Department has utilized the Digital EMS Solutions,
  Incorporated Medic Clipboard software package since 2011. The yearly total
  cost for the Medic Clipboard package is based on the actual number of reports
  (units) generated. Each report is billed at a rate of $5.50 per unit (PPU) and the
  San Gabriel Fire Department enjoys a discounted rate of $4.85 per unit. In
  addition to the PPU, the City pays a fee of $0.10 per PPU to fax run sheets from
  the system server to the base hospital per Los Angeles County Ref. 607 policy.
  The $4.85 PPU charge is recovered as part of the Dispatch Fee charged for each
  call per the current fee schedule. The total estimated cost per year is $10,817
  for Fiscal Year 2024-2025 and $10,766.25 for the subsequent two years through
  Fiscal Year 2026-2027 and is captured in the Fire Department Contractual
  Services Account No. 121-761-00-22-000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Fire Chief to execute a
  new three-year agreement with Digital EMS Solutions, Inc. to continue
  providing ePCR and EMS record management at the rates outlined on
  Attachment “B”.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 16, 2024  7
   5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. APPROVAL OF PLACEMENT OF VETERAN’S MEMORIAL DISPLAY

  San Gabriel Veterans’ Memorial Coalition (SGVMC) was established in 2020
  for the purpose of honoring San Gabriel’s veterans and working toward the
  development of a memorial in San Gabriel. Throughout the last two years,
  staff has met with the group and worked with them to determine a location
  for the memorial. The group has had various leaders and has worked to
  identify a design for the memorial. The group initially proposed a location
  in Smith Park, but more recently has decided on a preferred location in Plaza
  Park. The selected site is under the palm trees in Plaza Park and is near the
  locations where we have held the Veterans Day and Memorial Day events.
  Approval of the proposed memorial location does not have a fiscal impact.
  Should the location be approved, staff has discussed that the City may cover
  the cost of the Veteran’s Memorial to honor the military branches and
  SGVMC could fund Phase 2 of the memorial, including names of those who
  served. Staff will come forward at a future meeting with a proposed
  Veteran’s Memorial and proposed budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the proposed location in
  Plaza Park and direct staff to identify an architect or monument company to draft
  a potential design for both phases of the memorial.

  B. ACCEPTANCE OF CANNABIS TAX FUND GRANT PROGRAM (CTFGP)
  FUNDING IN THE AMOUNT OF $184,978.00 [RESOLUTION NO. 24-38]

  On behalf of the California Highway Patrol (CHP), the San Gabriel Police
  Department has been awarded grant funds from the Cannabis Tax Fund
  Grant Program (CTFGP) in the amount of $184,978. The purpose of the
  CTFGP is to provide alternative funding sources to augment, but not
  supplant, current activities and programs. The CHP will allocate funds for
  the project categories in accordance with the California Code of Regulations
  Sections 1890.05 through 1890.07, as determined by the CHP. Per the

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 16, 2024  8
   attached resolution, fund 186 (Other Grants) revenue estimates for Fiscal
  Year 2024-2025 will be increased by $184,978 as part of the acceptance of
  the grant funding. Additionally, budget appropriations will be increased to
  expend the funds, which will be expended out of Special Project Account
  No. 124-751-57-99-383.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the following:

  1. Increase estimated revenue (transfers in) and appropriations in (Account
  No. 124-751-57-99-383).

  2. Authorize the Police Chief to accept the Cannabis Tax Fund Grant
  Program funding to purchase the authorized items under the City’s
  purchasing policy and to administer the program according to the
  program’s guidelines.

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement between the City
  and California Highway Patrol and adopt Resolution No. 24-38
  amending the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Operating Budget.

  C. DISCUSSION REGARDING SHORT-TERM RENTALS AND RELATED FEES,
  STANDARDS AND REGULATIONS

  The City Council requested that staff bring forward a discussion on short-
  term rentals within the City of San Gabriel. Short-term rentals (those of less
  than 30 days) are not fully addressed in the Municipal Code outside of two
  newly-adopted Codes. The Accessory Dwelling Unit Ordinance allows for
  tenancy of over 30 days pursuant to State and local laws. Municipal Code
  Section 153.048 Urban Dwelling Units and Urban Lot Splits prohibits short-
  term rentals, which are rental units that provide less than a 30-day tenancy.
  The intent of this report is to seek direction from Council regarding potential
  fees, standards, and regulations that may be imposed on such uses. There
  are no known fiscal impacts for this project.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 16, 2024  9
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the matter of short-term
  rentals and direct staff to continue to ban short-term rentals and bring back
  code amendments to modernize our short-term rental ban.

  D. HUMAN RESOURCES DEPARTMENT UPDATE

  The primary mission of the Human Resources Department is to recruit,
  develop, and protect the City’s most valuable resource, its employees. The
  Department manages several organizational programs and functions
  including insurance and risk management, organizational development,
  employee recruitment and retention, compensation and benefits, and
  training and development. This presentation will provide an overview of the
  duties, accomplishments, ongoing projects, and future objectives of the
  Department.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  This is an informational item only; no action is required.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members
  to report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, August 20, 2024
  at 6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting
  will be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s
  website at www.sangabrielcity.com.
